why: Two more of dotenv's ten findings are `README.md:122` and `:132`, and both are the same documented example: a `PRIVATE_KEY=` whose value opens with the BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY line, closes with the END one, and whose body between them is literally elided with `...`. There is no key there. The `chave-privada` rule matches the OPENING LINE and only it -- which is right, that line is public and is what makes the finding cheap to spot -- but it means the span handed to the placeholder is that line, which is never a placeholder, and the evidence is in the BODY, on other lines. That is why the placeholder now takes the file's lines. THE TEST IS ABOUT SHAPE, NOT ABOUT VOCABULARY, and both halves have to hold: key material is base64 in long runs, an elision is short runs plus an ellipsis. The fail side is the same document, the same two fences and the same two spellings -- and it carries an ellipsis TOO, in the middle of a body of real shape, which is what a person does when they paste a real key into documentation and cut the middle out. Those 64-character lines are still key material and the finding stands. Whoever keeps only the ellipsis test and drops the run test turns that fail side green; whoever drops the whole mechanism turns the pass side red.
